newsitem.title: south africa: GOLF-MCNULTY CLOSES IN ON DA SILVA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCNULTY CLOSES IN ON DA SILVA.

text.p: Brazilian Adilson da Silva was unable reproduce the deft putting touch of his opening round, allowing Mark McNulty to move within a shot of him in the South African Masters on Friday.
Da Silva, four shots clear of the field after the first day, shot a one-under-par 71 for a 36-hole aggregate of 138.
Zimbabwean McNulty gathered four birdies in a faultless round of 68 at a wet and windy San Lameer Country Club.
McNulty moved to three-under for the tournament with an outward nine of 34. He then birdied the 11th and 13th to share the lead with da Silva but was unable to pick up any further shots.
Da Silva played solidly from tee to green but missed several putts between six and 10 feet for birdies.
"My putter wasn't at all hot today -- maybe I was trying too hard instead of just letting it happen," he said.
South African Desvonde Botes found the conditions very much to his liking. A course record 65 lifted him up the leaderboard to third place on 141.
